en.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak exceeds 11,000 cases
en.dek: International aid for DR Congo Ebola response fails to reach front lines as Kenya marks 42-day countdown to Ebola-free status.
facts: DR Congo Ebola outbreak has surpassed 11,000 total cases with 5,387 deaths.
International aid funds are not reaching the front lines of the DR Congo Ebola response.
Kenya discharged its last Ebola patient on 11 November.
Kenya began a 42-day countdown to being declared Ebola-free.
Kenya recorded nine confirmed Ebola cases during the outbreak.
Attacks on health workers are hindering Ebola containment in eastern DR Congo.
body: Democratic Republic of the Congo authorities announced on 11 November that the Ebola outbreak has surpassed 11,000 total cases, Al Jazeera reported that the virus has resulted in 5,387 deaths.
MedicalXpress and Al Jazeera confirmed these figures represent the highest number of cases recorded in the country's history for this virus.
Doctors Without Borders (MSF) reported on 12 November that international aid funds intended for the DR Congo Ebola response are not reaching the front lines.
The medical charity stated that staff are going unpaid and lack essential supplies as the virus continues to spread.
BBC and AllAfrica reported that these financial issues are hindering the containment of the virus in affected regions.
The reports indicated that the lack of resources is impacting the ability of medical teams to operate effectively.
Kenya discharged its last Ebola patient on 11 November, Health Minister Aden Duale said.
The country began a 42-day countdown to being declared Ebola-free, provided no new cases are recorded.
BBC and The Straits Times reported that the discharge marks a step towards the country achieving virus-free status.
DW and Der Spiegel confirmed that Kenya recorded nine total cases during the outbreak.
Africa CDC warns that attacks on health workers and facilities are increasingly hindering efforts to contain the Ebola outbreak in eastern DR Congo, which has killed more than 5,400 people.
The New York Times reports Israeli authorities say Hamas established a command center at the hospital complex.

de.dek: Internationale Hilfsgelder für die Ebola-Bekämpfung in der Demokratischen Republik Kongo erreichen die Frontlinien nicht, während Kenia einen 42-tägigen Countdown bis zur Erklärung der Ebola-Freiheit beginnt.
body: Ärzte ohne Grenzen (MSF) berichtete am 12. November, dass internationale Hilfsgelder, die für die Ebola-Bekämpfung in der Demokratischen Republik Kongo bestimmt sind, die Frontlinien nicht erreichen. Die medizinische Hilfsorganisation erklärte, dass Mitarbeiter nicht bezahlt werden und es an lebensnotwendigen Versorgungsgütern mangelt, während sich das Virus weiter ausbreitet.

BBC und AllAfrica berichteten, dass diese finanziellen Probleme die Eindämmung des Virus in den betroffenen Regionen behindern. Die Berichte wiesen darauf hin, dass der Mangel an Ressourcen die effektive Arbeitsfähigkeit der medizinischen Teams beeinträchtigt.

Die Behörden der Demokratischen Republik Kongo gaben am 11. November bekannt, dass der Ebola-Ausbruch insgesamt 11.000 Fälle überschritten hat. Laut Gesundheitsministerium und Al Jazeera hat das Virus zu 5.387 Todesfällen geführt.

Al Jazeera berichtete, dass diese Zahlen die höchste jemals im Land verzeichnete Anzahl an Fällen für dieses Virus darstellen. MedicalXpress erklärte, dass die Gesundheitsbehörden bei der Eindämmung der Virusausbreitung vor erheblichen Schwierigkeiten stehen.

Kenia entließ am 11. November seinen letzten Ebola-Patienten, wie Gesundheitsminister Aden Duale mitteilte. Das Land begann einen 42-tägigen Countdown bis zur Erklärung der Ebola-Freiheit, sofern keine neuen Fälle verzeichnet werden.

BBC und The Straits Times berichteten, dass die Entlassung einen Schritt in Richtung des virusfreien Status des Landes markiert. DW und Der Spiegel bestätigten, dass Kenia während des Ausbruchs insgesamt neun Fälle verzeichnete.

BBC described the discharge as a major milestone towards virus-free status in the region. The Straits Times reported the countdown as a step towards disease-free status, and DW reported that the patient left hospital.
DW and Der Spiegel reported that Kenya had nine confirmed Ebola cases, and both reports were published on 11 November 2026. The figure reflects the confirmed infections in the country.

Al Jazeera reported that these figures represent the highest number of cases recorded in the country's history for this virus, as stated by government officials.
MedicalXpress reported that health officials are facing significant difficulties in containing the spread of the virus as teams work in affected regions.
